text: Do not let your vanity and self-love make you suppose that people become your friends at first sight, or even upon a short acquaintance. Real friendship is a slow grower and never thrives unless engrafted upon a stock of known and reciprocal merit.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XVI, to his son, London, October 9, Old Style 1747
